metaData.originalTitle: Lionel Messi — improbably， still as good as ever
metaData.title: Lionel Messi — improbably， still as good as ever
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article examines Lionel Messi's remarkable form at age 38 during the 2026 World Cup, analyzing his preparation, fitness, and enduring brilliance through interviews and behind-the-scenes details.
metaData.summary: A deep-dive analysis of Lionel Messi's performance and preparation for the 2026 World Cup, where he scored a hat-trick against Algeria in Argentina's opener. The piece traces his journey from uncertainty about participating, through a demanding training regimen with Argentina teammate Rodrigo De Paul and Inter Miami's internal 'Super Liga' competition, to his injury scare and rapid recovery. Featuring quotes from Scaloni, Xavi, Haaland, and anonymous sources, it explores Messi's diet, fitness adaptation to MLS, and the family-like atmosphere of the Argentina camp. The article argues that Messi, improbably, remains as good as ever, driven by competitiveness and meticulous physical preparation.

mainPoints.point: Messi's hat-trick on his 200th Argentina appearance proved his enduring quality.
mainPoints.explanation: At 38, he equaled Miroslav Klose's all-time World Cup goal record and delivered a vintage performance against Algeria.

mainPoints.point: Messi's preparation was unusually rigorous, including double sessions with De Paul.
mainPoints.explanation: To prove himself on merit, Messi followed a tailored training plan beyond club commitments, focusing on peak physical condition.

mainPoints.point: Inter Miami's internal competition helped maintain his sharpness before the World Cup.
mainPoints.explanation: The 'Super Liga' small-sided tournament saw Messi score over 80 goals, far exceeding teammates, and his form carried into MLS regular season.

mainPoints.point: Argentina's setup—from coaching to AI-driven monitoring—supports Messi's longevity.
mainPoints.explanation: The AFA uses data tracking for injury prevention and nutrition, and Physio Walter Insaurralde works with Messi in Miami to fine-tune his body.

mainPoints.point: Messi's competitive drive, not just talent, explains his continued excellence.
mainPoints.explanation: Quotes from Scaloni, Xavi, and Haaland emphasize his relentless will to compete and adapt, even after winning the 2022 World Cup.

keyQuotes: I could stay here with you for over an hour trying to explain what he does. But you need to be there to really understand the atmosphere, the ambience.
'The little fella! He's so up for it!'
'Lionel Messi's final World Cup match surely'... And yet look who it is. Messi is still here.
